note: Adapted from the original English description of Snyder 1924 (new species, Leucotermes cardini Snyder, type locality Andros Island, Bahamas; later placed in Heterotermes). The passages available here cover the first half of the alate; the wing venation and the continuation of the measurements were not included in the extract. The original notes that the soldier is difficult to separate from convexinotatus on the soldier alone, the soldier of cardini having more hairs on the head.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: New species (originally Leucotermes cardini, later placed in Heterotermes). Type locality Andros Island, Bahamas; also recorded from Cuba. Alate head pale yellowish brown, darker between the compound eyes; antennae 17-segmented; compound eyes black, not round, slightly protruding; labrum and postclypeus as in L. convexinotatus; pronotum nearly heart-shaped, the middle of the anterior margin concave, the posterior margin slightly concave; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum not concave, the mesonotum covered by wing scales. The soldier has more hairs on the head than convexinotatus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head pale yellowish brown, darker between the compound eyes and paler posteriorly; nearly oval, widest at the compound eyes, rounded posteriorly; covered with dense long and short hairs. Fontanelle a pale, slightly raised round spot on the line behind the compound eyes. Antennae pale yellow, 17-segmented, with short hairs, the segments varying in size and shape; first segment long, cylindrical; second shorter than the first; third ring-like, about half the length of the second; fourth ring-like, longer than the third; last segment long, slender, elliptical. Compound eyes black, not round, slightly protruding; their distance from the lateral margin of the head less than (or equal to) their long diameter. Ocelli present or absent, their distance from the compound eyes about equal to the short diameter of an ocellus. Labrum and postclypeus as in L. convexinotatus. Pronotum concolorous with the head, nearly heart-shaped, the middle of the anterior margin concave, the posterior margin slightly concave, with long and short hairs. Posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum not concave; the mesonotum covered by wing scales. Legs pale yellow, slender and long. Wings smoky, the costa yellow, the wing margins with marginal hairs, the wing surface punctate, with few hairs on the surface.
